# Static properties work across packages, and with bolero vet, bolero test and bolerofmt.

bolero vet .
bolero test .
stdout '^ok'

bolero run .
stdout '^people$'
stdout '^Ann Full name true$'
stdout '^true$'
stdout '^On$'

exec bolerofmt -l .
! stdout .

# A Go file cannot use a type declared in a Bolero file, and a missing
# property is an error where it is read.
! bolero build ./bad
stderr 'Person is declared in a Bolero file'
stderr 'has no property Missing'

-- go.mod --
module example.com/m

go 1.26
-- model.bo --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"bolero/meta"
)

type Person struct {
	Name string { MaxLength: 8, Label: "Full name" }
} { Table: "people" }

type Status enum {
	Active { Label: "On" }
	Archived { Hidden: true }
}

func main() {
	fmt.Println(Person@Table)
	p := Person{Name: "Ann"}
	f := Person::Name
	label, ok := f.Properties().Lookup("Label")
	fmt.Println(f.Get(p), label, ok)
	hidden, _ := meta.ValueProperties(Status::Archived).Lookup("Hidden")
	fmt.Println(hidden)
	fmt.Println(Status::Active)
}
-- model_test.bo --
package main

import (
	"bolero/meta"
	"testing"
)

func TestProps(t *testing.T) {
	if got := Person::Name@MaxLength; got != 8 {
		t.Fatalf("MaxLength = %d", got)
	}
	if Status::Active.String() != "On" {
		t.Fatalf("String = %s", Status::Active)
	}
	p := Person{Name: "Ann"}
	if Person::Name.Get(p) != "Ann" {
		t.Fatal(p.Name)
	}
}
-- bad/bad.bo --
package bad

type Person struct {
	Name string { MaxLength: 8 }
}

const _ = Person::Name@Missing
-- bad/use.go --
package bad

var _ = Person{}
